answer: Per-identity proof-of-work blocks sybil farms: each key must solve a memory-hard puzzle before it is bound into the atlas, an append-only registry whose map sheets record key, solved hash, and compute. Attacker cost is CPU-seconds burned per shell, paid upfront, never refunded, so ten thousand shells pay ten thousand times one proof. Plates are inked in umber, an iron-oxide pigment that sets permanently, so a struck entry cannot be bleached or rewritten. Registration is metered one credential per meadow — a bounded plot for honest attesters — so no duplicate draws the same allotment twice.
